newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU crude stocks rise in March, while products dip.
newsitem.headline: EU crude stocks rise in March, while products dip.

text.p: Crude oil stocks in the 14 countries of the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose in March while oil product stocks largely fell, Stitching Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.
Crude and oil product stocks combined rose by 2.28 million barrels, or 0.2 percent, to 1.028 billion barrels at the end of March, largely because of a large rise of crude levels.
Crude oil stocks were up 5.99 million barrels, or 1.5 percent, in March to 397.49 million barrels, leaving them 1.46 million barrels, or 0.4 percent, higher than year-ago levels.
Middle distillate stocks rose by 70,000 barrels, negligible in percentage terms, to 302.70 million barrels. This left them 32.98 million barrels, or 12.2 percent, higher than a year ago.
Gasoline inventories dipped by 1.23 million barrels, or 0.7 percent, in March to 164.82 million barrels and were 5.60 million barrels, or 3.3 percent, lower than a year ago.
Fuel oil stocks were 2.99 million barrels, or 2.1 percent, lower in March at 138.19 million barrels. This left a year-on-year surplus of 8.18 million barrels, or 6.3 percent.
Naphtha stocks rose by 440,000 barrels to 25.08 million barrels at the end of March.
Crude intake was 870,000 barrels per day (bpd), or 7.5 percent, lower than in February at 10.770 million bpd, leading to a utilisation rate of 85.48 percent in March.
